name: Friction hair removal mitt (buffing)

lead: A friction hair removal mitt is a rough, abrasive pad or glove that is rubbed over the skin to wear hair away at the surface. People use it to get smooth skin on legs, arms or body for a cleaner look without razors or wax.
Friction is a recognised depilation method, meaning it removes hair at or above the skin surface, so regrowth appears within hours to days. The Egyptians used pumice for a similar purpose.

paras: The mitt is typically rubbed over dry or damp skin in circular or back-and-forth strokes until hair is worn down. Because it works at the surface, results are temporary.
Hair removal in general can cause skin inflammation, minor burns, ingrown hairs, bumps and folliculitis. Abrasive rubbing on skin may add to irritation.

angle.text: The mitt wears hair off at the skin surface for a temporary smooth finish.

lead: Friction hair removal uses a rough surface, such as pumice or an abrasive pad or mitt, to buff hair away at skin level [1]. It is classed as depilation, which removes hair at or above the surface rather than at the root, and lasts several hours to several days [1].
People use it to get smoother-looking skin without shaving or waxing. Hair removal methods in general can cause skin inflammation, ingrown hairs and folliculitis [1].

paras: Friction is listed among depilation methods and described as rough surfaces used to buff away hair; pumice use dates to ancient Egypt [1].
Reported effects of hair removal generally include skin inflammation, minor burns, lesions, scarring, ingrown hairs, bumps and folliculitis [1].
